newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Delta says Hartley to cost US$287 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Delta says Hartley to cost US$287 mln.

text.p: Delta Gold NL said on Monday the estimated capital cost of the joint venture Hartley platinum mine in Zimbabwe had now risen to US$287 million.

Delta foreshadowed a rise in the total capital cost from the previous estimate of US$264 million in its September quarter report. The revised forecast, prepared by manager The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, was due mainly to changes arising from a detailed design of the base metal refinery, it said.
Delta said first metal production was still expected in mid-calendar 1997. BHP now expected the build-up to full production at the project to take about 15 months, it said.
Throughput of 90,000 tonnes per month was scheduled for September 1997, and the full 180,000 tonnes per month for September 1998.
Delta said the revised schedule for mining, plant commissioning and build-up of production took into account safety requirements and delays mentioned previously.
The company has referred earlier to temporary visa problems for a number of expatriate staff, and delays in commissioning a processing plant.

Delta said the mining schedule had also been adversely affected by delays in build-up to full production in the South mine caused by a deeper-than-expected but localised zone of weathering. BHP has 67 per cent of the Hartley platinum project, while Delta has the remaining 33 per cent.
Hartley is expected to produce 150,000 ounces of platinum a year, 115,000 ounces of palladium, 11,500 ounces of rhodium and 23,000 ounces of gold, as well as some copper and nickel.
